correctness.rationale: For any side point, strict convexity of squared distance on each polygon edge reduces the farthest-boundary maximization exactly to all vertices. The full circle vertex grid at angles (2k+1)pi/n shows the nearest-to-antipode vertex is at angle pi when n is odd and one of the two bracketing angles pi±pi/n when n is even. Explicit coordinate squared distances give the two complete piecewise profiles on the entire closed side. Their defects from the squared midpoint value are t^2 and t^2+2R sin(pi/n)|t|, respectively; unique center locations and farthest endpoints follow. Perimeter ratios and stated asymptotics are exact algebra; verify.py rechecks the expansions and all vertices at 401880 sample comparisons.
risks: The finite numerical vertex comparisons are diagnostic, not a substitute for the all-integer angular-ordering proof.
The odd-order fixed-vertex-number global minimizing conjecture remains unproved by this result.

originality.rationale: The original 2016 full preprint contains only a generic finite polygon algorithm and small-n benchmarks. The materially read 2021 full journal paper computes arbitrary triangles and maximizers of a different perimeter problem, without a regular-n-gon family profile. The 2023 full preprint devotes its main proof to quadrilaterals and in Section 9 proposes odd regular n-gons as possible global minimizers, without an exact complete boundary profile. No compared record or located prior source contains the all-n farthest-distance function or sharp parity-dependent boundary-center stability; the known n=3 and n=4 scalar values and the coincident even-polygon diameter-bisection numerical expression are credited as prior, not claimed separately.

value.rationale: The invariant is central to a recently active sharp perimeter-at-fixed-self-radius program. A 2023 primary paper specifically conjectures that regular odd n-gons minimize perimeter for every odd n (proved for n=3 only). The all-order exact candidate coefficient is therefore a natural necessary benchmark for that open program; more substantially, the continuous farthest-distance profile uniquely characterizes all constrained minimax centers and farthest endpoints. The exact stability law distinguishes quadratic smooth odd minima from linear cusps at even minima, information unavailable from the scalar radius and mathematically meaningful for optimizing and perturbing boundary centers. No global extremal theorem is claimed.
risks: Closed formulas in a highly symmetric family can be elementary; value rests specifically on their role as complete benchmark and sharp profile for the stated open problem, not on algebraic difficulty.
